title: EXLdata.ai for banking
body_markdown:
EXLdata.ai is a modular, agentic data-management framework. Its specialized agents interpret data, code, metadata, logs, and documents. It connects these items through lineage, semantic models, and knowledge graphs, then make that context available for modernization, governance, analytics, and AI. These capabilities can be deployed individually or combined around priority banking outcomes.


#### Data engineering


Automates ingestion, mapping, transformation and validation across batch, streaming, API, and change-data-capture pipelines. Banks can integrate deposits, lending, cards, and payments data, build governed risk and finance data products, and accelerate onboarding to cloud and lakehouse platforms.


#### Data migration


Discovers dependencies, generates source-to-target mappings, converts legacy logic, and reconciles data with traceable evidence. This supports legacy warehouse, Hadoop, and core-platform modernization while reducing cutover, integrity, and control risks.


#### Data quality


Profiles data, detects anomalies and duplicates, applies business rules, and supports governed remediation. This strengthens AML and KYC completeness, CCAR and stress-testing controls, credit-risk inputs, transaction reconciliation, and regulatory reporting.


#### Data annotation and curation


Extracts entities, attributes, and relationships from documents, notes, and other unstructured information, seeking human validation where needed. This helps banks activate KYC and onboarding documents, loan files, adverse-media inputs, relationship-manager notes, and investigation evidence.


#### Master and reference data management


Matches, merges, and governs customer, product, account, and reference data using stewardship, survivorship, and harmonization rules. It supports consistent customer and household identity, merchant identity, product hierarchies, legal entities, and standardized risk and finance codes.


#### Data governance and lineage


Automates metadata capture, classification, ownership, and policy controls. Multi-system lineage connects code, pipelines, platforms, and reports, tracing critical data elements through transformations to authoritative systems of record. This supports BCBS 239, regulatory-report mapping, consent-order remediation, change-impact analysis, and audit evidence.


#### Ontology and knowledge graph


Connects banking entities, relationships, policies, metrics, and data assets into shared business context. By linking customers, accounts, transactions, merchants, and risk signals, it gives analytics and AI agents the context needed for AML and fraud investigations, relationship intelligence, and explainable decision support.


#### Semantic layer


Creates governed definitions, metrics, synonyms, and relationships that can be reused across dashboards, query tools, and AI agents. Consistent definitions for exposure, balance, delinquency, approval rate, and transaction volume help users and agents receive reliable, explainable answers regardless of how a question is phrased.


#### DataOps and observability


Monitors pipeline health, freshness, quality, schema drift, dependencies, and service levels, with proactive alerts and impact analysis. This improves the resilience of regulatory-data pipelines, payment feeds, fraud-model inputs, overnight risk processes, and critical finance workloads.
